text: Circumference, Area, Arc Length, Sectors, Radians, Velocity, and Solid Figures

slides.title: Learning Goals
text: By the end of this lesson, you will be able to:
Name and define radius, diameter, chord, tangent, secant, arc, sector, and segment.
Find areas of triangles, parallelograms, trapezoids, piecewise figures, and concentric circle regions.
Convert between DMS, decimal degrees, and radians.
Apply s = rθ, A = ½r²θ, and v = rω to solve problems.
Use formulas for prisms, cylinders, cones, spheres, and pyramids.

slides.title: Piecewise Rectangular Figures
text: Break complex shapes into rectangles, find each area, then add them together.

slides.title: Circle Terminology
text: A circle is the set of all points in a plane equidistant from a fixed point (the center).
Center to circle. Half the diameter.
Segment with both endpoints on circle.
Line touching circle at exactly one point.
Line intersecting circle at two points.

slides.title: Arcs, Sectors & Segments
text: Key regions and curves defined within a circle.
A portion of the circumference. Minor arc < semicircle; major arc > semicircle.
Angle at the center formed by two radii. Its measure equals the intercepted arc.
The "pie-slice" region between two radii and the arc they intercept.
The region between a chord and its arc. A chord creates a minor and major segment.

slides.title: Circumference & Area
text: Two fundamental measurements of every circle.
The space enclosed by the circle. Always use the radius.
Leave answers in terms of π for exact answers. Use π ≈ 3.14159 for decimal approximations.

slides.title: Area Between Concentric Circles
text: When one circle is inside another sharing the same center, the ring-shaped region between them is called an annulus.
R = outer radius, r = inner radius
A circular fountain has radius 4 ft. A walkway 3 ft wide
surrounds it. Find the area of the walkway.

slides.title: Inscribed Angles
text: An inscribed angle has its vertex on the circle and its sides are chords.
The measure of an inscribed angle is exactly one-half the measure of its intercepted arc.
An inscribed angle in a semicircle is always 90°, because the intercepted arc is 180°.

slides.title: Chord & Angle Theorems
text: When two chords intersect inside a circle, the angles formed relate to the intercepted arcs.
The angle equals half the sum of the two intercepted arcs.
A diameter divides the circle into two semicircles of 180° each.

slides.title: Worked Example: Circle Angles
text: ∠AED = 133° and arc AB = 52°. AC is a diameter (BD is not). Find ∠AEB, ∠ACB, and arc CD.
133° = ½(arc AD + arc BC). Arc BC = 180° − 52° = 128°

slides.title: Degrees, Minutes & Seconds
text: Angles in navigation and surveying use DMS notation. 1° = 60′ (minutes), 1′ = 60″ (seconds).
Divide minutes by 60, seconds by 3600, then add all parts.

slides.title: Degrees & Radians
text: If a central angle intercepts an arc equal in length to the radius, that angle is exactly 1 radian.
One radian ≈ 57.296°. Think of it as the angle that "unwraps" one radius-length of arc.

slides.title: Arc Length
text: The distance along the curved part of a circle between two points. θ must be in radians.
Convert to radians first by multiplying by π/180,
s = arc length, r = radius, θ = central angle (radians)

slides.title: Area of a Sector
text: A sector is the "pie-slice" region between two radii and an arc. Its area is proportional to θ.
This is simply the fraction of the full circle's area.
A = area, r = radius, θ = central angle (radians)

slides.title: Real-World Sector Problems
text: Applying arc length and sector area to aviation and everyday scenarios.
Arc south on 12 NM arc from 090 to 210 radial.
TLAR check: 120° is ⅓ of 360°, so ⅓ × 2π(12) ≈ 25 NM ✓
A sprinkler sprays water 20 ft, covering a 150° sector.
Find the area of the watered region.
That is about 150/360 ≈ 41.7% of the full circle.

slides.title: S E C T I O N 3
text: Connecting rotational speed to the speed of a point on a spinning object.

slides.title: Linear & Angular Velocity
text: Two ways to describe how fast something spins — and how they connect.
How fast the angle changes. Measured in rad/s or rad/min.
Speed of a point on the rotating object. Farther from center → faster.
1 revolution = 2π radians. So n RPM = n × 2π rad/min. Always convert before using v = rω.
Key insight: v = rω — linear velocity is directly proportional to both radius and angular velocity.
